video_title: Ant's injury | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' knee injury and the decision to delay surgery
quotes.excerpt: It does seem like here is how kind of the whole summer and the whole issue unfolded.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Let's get right into it. Anthony Edwards' injury. Let's deal with there's always a conspiratorial aspect to every major story these days. Let's deal with the first reaction of so many Timberwolves fans. Why didn't he do it this summer? Is that a realistic criticism?

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: Certainly when you look at it right away and you see that Anthony Edwards was clearly early on in this season playing through some discomfort in his knee. He dealt with knee injuries in the playoffs last season and you say, of course, why wouldn't he have just done it in June and taken the whole summer to get ready? Talking to people with Anthony Edwards, with the Timberwolves last night, it does seem like here is how kind of the whole summer and the whole issue unfolded. One is, right after the Spurs series was over, Anthony Edwards and the team met, talked about the injury that he was dealing with. Remember he had two knee injuries at that time. He had a hyperextended left knee and then he had basically what's called runner's knee, inflammation in his right knee that was really bothering him. The left knee right now is fine. Everything is good there with the hyperextension. It is the right knee that needs this new surgery. Edwards met with the medical staff, with the training staff, and collectively they came up with the plan that, hey, we can just rest this injury and if you take some real time off this summer, you are going to be okay going into next season.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: New MRI results necessitated Anthony Edwards' knee surgery
quotes.excerpt: They got new imaging with an MRI, and it revealed a worse situation than had been examined.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: They get to Miami in the season opener and he's playing and playing well, but from what I'm told at some point in that game, there was a tweak of some sort that happened with his right knee. They got new imaging with an MRI, and it revealed a worse situation than had been examined this last summer in July, I think was the previous examination. And so at that point, Ant was still such a competitive guy, he's like, I think I can play through this. I think it's a pain management situation. I want to be out there for the team. Let's see what's going on. And then, he goes through the next few games, it is still bothering him. We signed against Toronto on Sunday, he was kind of grabbing at his knee and grimacing. He played in a back-to-back in Cleveland, plays 41 minutes, scores 47 points, is very, very effective, but I think at that time coming out of that game, from what I understand, it was another meeting with Timberwolves doctors. When they got back to Minneapolis from Cleveland, and at that time it was determined that, hey, we've got to address this some way, somehow. And so, this is not the exact same injury that he was dealing with in the summertime right after the Spurs series.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' mindset regarding his upcoming knee surgery
quotes.excerpt: He's obviously disappointed by having to have this procedure. It will take him out of MVP consideration.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Do you have a sense from other people what his mindset is right now?

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: Yes, so what I'm told he's in good spirits. He's obviously disappointed by having to have this procedure. It will take him out of MVP all-NBA consideration and there's financial implications to that as well as competitive implications for the Timberwolves, but I think he's taking it fairly in stride. The one thing that was told to me about this and not just trying to play through it was he looks at the way this team has come together, how quickly they have gelled, his chemistry with LaMelo, how Kuminga is playing, just everything around it and the great start that they've gotten off to, and he really believes that this is a team that can go deep into the playoffs and that can come out of the Western Conference.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Anthony Edwards' injury impacts potential supermax contract eligibility
quotes.excerpt: He came into this season needing an MVP or an all-NBA or defensive player of the year.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Take us through the financial and contract ramifications with all-NBA and how that plays into him coming toward the end of his deal.

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: So remember last year, Jim, he missed all-NBA by just a couple of games because of some injuries that he dealt with. And so, he came into this season needing an MVP or an all-NBA or defensive player of the year award to trigger the ability for the Timberwolves to offer a supermax extension, which would have been a four-year deal in the area of $304 million that would have started in 2029 and 30 and extended his contract from there. Because he will not meet the games threshold to qualify for that, he could still sign an extension for less money than that, but we don't know exactly how the team and he will approach that if he'll want to just extend and have some financial security for himself, or if he can go into the following season and try and get an all-NBA honor, you know, next season and then get back into the running for the supermax eligibility.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Ito Dosunmu's emergence as a starter and vocal leader
quotes.excerpt: Ito Dosunmu is probably the clear first or most obvious choice to put in the starting lineup.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: What's this team going to look like without Ant? Is Ito going to go in the starting lineup? How does that change the dynamics of the bench players, who gets more minutes, and how well can they survive this?

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: So I think like when you look at the ramifications from taking out their best player, you have Ito Dosunmu is probably the clear first or most obvious choice to put in the starting lineup. He is a combo guard. He has played exceedingly well to start this season on both ends of the floor. And Jim, I think the other argument for Ito in the starting lineup is that he has kind of really emerged as a vocal leader on this team. If you talk to guys about who is running the shows in practice and who is being really influential behind the scenes and in the locker room, Ito Dosunmu has really stepped into kind of the hole that was vacated by Mike Conley, Kyle Anderson leaving. And so, he has a ton of respect from his teammates and so bringing him into that starting lineup would certainly from a sheer presence factor give the Wolves something there.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Terrence Shannon Jr. as a potential starter in Anthony Edwards' absence
quotes.excerpt: There is a possibility that Chris Finch could go to Terrence Shannon Jr., another player who played well.

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: There is a possibility that Chris Finch could go to Terrence Shannon Jr., another player who played well, a slightly different physical profile from Ito, and it might be like if you want to argue that let's keep Ito in the sixth man role and kind of keep the rotation as close to normal as possible, maybe you do go TSJ there, but I would guess it's going to be Ito Dosunmu. Either way, you have two bigger wings that have played well this this season in the early going. And so, of course, Anthony Edwards losing him and his incredible scoring that he was showing, 45 against Miami, 47 against Cleveland, that is an enormous loss, but they do have some depth on the wing to to kind of mitigate that for the short term.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' rebounding strength and the Cleveland game performance
quotes.excerpt: We went into the season thinking that the fatal flaw for this team might be rebounding.

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: If Ant hadn't been injured, two things I would have wanted to get to first in this show today. Number one, we went into the season thinking that the fatal flaw for this team might be rebounding, and they are destroying people on the boards. And number two, I liked pretty much everything I saw out of the first four games, except third quarter against Cleveland. I thought the ball stopped moving and it was like LaMelo Ball didn't exist and Ant was just going to play one-on-one. I didn't like that. Even though he was very productive, I didn't love the way that looked. Let's go with the rebounding first. How surprised are you that they're rebounding this well and will that category still be a strength with Ant out?

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves overcoming rebounding concerns without a muscle surplus
quotes.excerpt: That has not just not been a weakness, it's been an incredible strength for them.
quotes.quote: I'm certainly surprised and I can tell you, I think people internally, coaches, executives are surprised as well that it's gone as overwhelmingly positive as it has. There was real concern going into this season about how the Wolves were going to hold up on the offensive and defensive glass without that muscle surplus that they had with Julius Randle and with Naz Reid. But that has not just not been a weakness, it's been an incredible strength for them.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves playing with a new ferocious mentality and collective rebounding effort
quotes.excerpt: This team has come out with just a ferocious mentality.
quotes.quote: This team has come out with just a ferocious mentality. Chris Finch has always said, what we have to do is get rebounding from everyone including the backcourt to help mitigate our size deficiency up front. And Rudy Gobert is rebounding unbelievably well. He had 20 rebounds against Cleveland. Jaden McDaniels is rebounding more. It's just a collective will that this team has shown this year that was not present last year.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Atmosphere and team energy during the home opener against Toronto
quotes.excerpt: The atmosphere in the building was electric. It was playoff-like. The place was absolutely full.

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: The thing that stood out to me about the home opener against Toronto on Sunday was that the atmosphere in the building was electric. It was playoff-like. The place was absolutely full. And the style of play for this team just had people out of their seats the whole game. And of course, you know, that includes LaMelo throwing a half-court lob to Baron Davis or LaMelo with the, you know, step-back three that he froze Colm Murray Boyle on and and and had a highlight reel thing. And that was it created a euphoric reaction from the fans. But I also really believe that the fan base has connected with this team because you can just see that they play really hard. And, you know, LaMelo is playing hard on defense. They are chasing guys in the backcourt. They are trying to force turnovers. They are getting out and running. Just from an aesthetic standpoint, you are watching this team and you're saying, man, these guys go and they care and they want to win and they are taking this seriously.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gobert's offensive struggles and potential rotation adjustments
quotes.excerpt: Why does Rudy struggle on the offensive end after so many years in the league?

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: I'm going to do this one, we're going to veer a little bit from the Ant subject for, for this question from the Lith P Bender. Why does Rudy struggle on the offensive end after so many years in the league?

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: We've been over a lot of Rudy's issues, but I do think that one thing that was apparent to me in the Cleveland game, he was 0 for 9 from the field, including he took two threes, one at the end of the shot clock. But I will say that it does appear to me at this stage of his career that his offensive limitations are exacerbated on the second nights of back-to-backs. And, you know, it seems like he's never he's not right now, he's not like a big motor skills guy that super smooth in operating on offense, but it does feel like when he is tired, when he is coming off of a game like that, he just everything slows down and so he's dropping the ball even more. He's having a little harder time elevating for lobs. And so, I think it might be a good idea to look at scaling back his minutes even a little bit more in those games, giving Yoan Berenge even more run. I think those that'd be a real possibility for for for Finch to to think about just to manage Rudy as a 34-year-old.
